name: multi-sdd-team
principles: The main session owns completion and may implement and remediate changes it owns.
Approved specifications and architecture decisions are reused; ambiguity or significant pending design decisions justify SDD, not file counts, line counts, or new tests.
Select specialists only for bounded investigation, independent implementation, or applicable review. Never spawn an orchestrator merely for classification unless requested.

Independent tasks may advance concurrently with separate ownership, worktrees or immutable snapshots. Never duplicate delegated work, edit the same files concurrently, or change a revision or shared environment under review.
No dependent stage starts until its applicable dependencies and required gates pass.
Conditional stages are mandatory when their canonical condition applies. Record why each conditional stage was included or skipped; a read-only task does not authorize code changes.
Demo-fast agent settings remain unchanged; speed never waives required architecture, security, or independent quality review.
Findings return to the implementation owner, checks rerun, and the originating reviewer revalidates the updated revision.
Architecture rules and exceptions require approval by the user or a designated human authority.
Architecture, quality, and security review gates emit pure governance JSON that must validate before dependent work continues. A valid envelope is not a passing gate decision.
Managed prompts under .codex/agents are immutable to every AI-mediated stage; only a human-controlled package update outside the agent workflow may replace them.

INLINE.description: Default direct execution by the main session, with applicable independent gates.

sequence.action: Independent report-only design gate on an immutable revision; validate JSON and require a passing decision before dependent implementation.

sequence.condition: Run only when the authorized task requires code or contract changes.

sequence.action: Independent report-only architecture compliance gate on the checked revision; validate JSON and honor unresolved findings.

hard_rules: Preserve explicit read-only, review-only, delivery and approval boundaries. Do not modify global configuration without authorization.
Reject any architecture_reviewer, tester_reviewer, or hacker handoff that is not valid agent-result JSON for the expected role and runtime.
Never treat invalid structured review output as a passing gate or continue to a dependent stage.
A required gate that failed, is invalid, remains unresolved, or was not run blocks dependent work and completion. Independent authorized work may continue.
Never start or delegate work when managed prompt protection is drifted, elevated, legacy, or unproven.
Never ask for escalation, invoke init or update, or delegate a bypass to modify .codex/agents.
Independent reviewers are report-only; implementation ownership and independent review ownership must remain separate.
Architecture rules and exceptions require explicit approval by the user or a designated human authority.
No strategy may waive a canonical condition because of size, speed, fast mode, or the presence of an approved specification.
Report observed blockers and uncertainty; avoid identical retries without new evidence or changed conditions. Never claim unexecuted environment or scenario validation.
Pipeline version 3 replaces version 2 routing and fixed specialist chains. These are static workflow declarations, not an operational scheduler or evidence that gates executed.
